title: Air India Express Flight From Dammam Diverted After Bomb Note Found in Lavatory
excerpt: All 40 passengers and crew were safely evacuated at Ahmedabad airport after a tissue paper bearing the words 'Bomb RED 4:30' was discovered in the aircraft's bathroom.
body:
• Air India Express flight IX-170 from Dammam to Delhi was diverted to Ahmedabad on Monday after a tissue paper bearing the words "Bomb RED 4:30" and a drawing of a bag was found in the aircraft's lavatory
  • All 32 passengers and 8 crew members were safely evacuated and frisked at Terminal 2 of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport
  • The Bomb Detection and Disposal Squad found no suspicious objects during their search of the aircraft
  • Police are investigating the origin of the handwritten note and the process of registering a criminal case is underway

A Dammam-to-Delhi Air India Express flight was diverted to Ahmedabad on Monday after the first officer discovered a tissue paper with a bomb threat inside the aircraft's lavatory, triggering emergency security protocols and the evacuation of all 40 people on board.

The Discovery

Flight IX-170, which departed from Dammam in Saudi Arabia at 10:25 a.m. local time, was en route to Delhi when the first officer found a tissue paper in the aircraft's bathroom carrying the words "Bomb RED 4:30" written in English, along with a sketch of a bag, according to a statement from Ahmedabad's Airport Police Station.

https://x.com/dna/status/2094476679683182619

The aircraft's Operation Control Centre informed authorities at approximately 2:40 p.m. that the flight was being diverted. The plane landed at Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport at 4:27 p.m. and was parked on the Terminal 2 taxiway, where police and security agencies immediately initiated prescribed security procedures.

Emergency Response

Police Inspector A.D. Chavda, accompanied by security personnel, reached Terminal 2 as the aircraft was being positioned. "A total of 32 passengers and eight members of the flight crew — four crew members and four air hostesses — were safely brought out of the aircraft and frisked," police said.

The government-appointed Bomb Threat Assessment Committee (BTAC) was alerted immediately, and the passengers and crew were subsequently checked by the Bomb Detection and Disposal Squad (BDDS). Police confirmed that no suspicious object had been found as of Monday evening.

"One of our flights from Dammam to Delhi was diverted to Ahmedabad as a precaution and in keeping with security protocols after being notified of a specific bomb threat. The flight landed, and all guests have been disembarked safely."

— Air India Express spokesperson

The aircraft has been kept in an isolated area at the airport while comprehensive checks continue. Airport authorities are also conducting necessary sanitation procedures as part of the standard response protocol.

Investigation Underway

Police said the investigation into the origin of the handwritten threat message is continuing. The process of registering a criminal offence in connection with the incident has been initiated, according to authorities.

Investigators are working to determine how the note was placed inside the aircraft and whether it constitutes a hoax. CCTV footage and passenger manifests are expected to be scrutinized as part of the probe. The flight will be allowed to depart once security checks and the investigation at the airport are completed, police said.

Gulf Route and Passenger Safety

The Dammam-Delhi route is among the busiest Gulf corridors for Indian travelers, connecting the large Indian expatriate community in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province with home. Air India Express operates frequent flights between Indian cities and Gulf destinations, carrying large numbers of diaspora workers and families.

The diversion comes amid a broader pattern of bomb hoax threats targeting Indian aviation. Ahmedabad itself has seen a spate of threat messages directed at its airport, courts, and schools in recent weeks, all of which were later found to be non-specific or hoaxes after extensive security checks, according to local reports.

Indian authorities have been tightening penalties for bomb hoaxes, which cause significant operational disruptions, divert security resources, and result in substantial financial losses for airlines while causing distress to passengers.
